exact_replacements.before: Art. 89 separately requires the immovable reference price to be determined under a ministerial order. This workpaper has not recovered that operative valuation instrument; a deed price alone does not prove the accepted taxable price. Calculations below explicitly assume the lawful price has already been established.
exact_replacements.after: Art. 89 requires the immovable reference price to follow a ministerial order. [Order 540/214bis of 5 March 2021, art. 17](https://amategeko.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BOB_No3-2021.pdf) points to Order 540/188 of 13 March 2000, completed by Order 540/577 of 31 July 2000. The recovered [signed Order 540/550/720/1145 of 27 February 2025, arts. 1–4](https://www.obr.bi/images/PDF/OM_PORTANT_ACTUALISATION_DES_TAUX_UTILISES_LORS_DE_LA_CESSION_IMMOBILIERE_OM_VALEURS_DE_CESSION_DES_PARCELLES_CENTRES_URBAINS_AU_29102026.pdf) implements 2024/25 budget art. 77: it defines reference values per are or square metre, provides the base for related duties/taxes and requires the higher contractual market value where that exceeds the calculated transfer value, without removing the authority's right to assess the real amount. Inputs depend on land location/surface and construction surface/materials/equipment, with its annexes integral. Arts. 6–7 repeal contrary earlier provisions and commence on signature; the filename's later date is not an enactment date. Continuing 2026 effect/current replacement and application to the actual property, including the relevant annex and inputs, are not established here. A deed price alone does not prove the accepted taxable price. Calculations below assume the lawful price has already been established.

exact_replacements.before: 5. **Apply only the corresponding registration-duty credit.** Match the land-registration duty evidence to the taxable gain.
exact_replacements.after: 5. **Apply only the seller-paid registration-duty credit.** Obtain proof that the seller paid the land-registration duties on that immovable sale and match them to the taxable gain. Buyer-paid duties do not become the seller's credit under Order 540/214bis art. 18.

exact_replacements.before: A buyer's acquisition-price withholding on a nonresident seller does not determine the seller's gain base. Apply the actual payment category, payer/recipient status and certificate route; do not assume all second-category tax is collected finally at source.
exact_replacements.after: A buyer's acquisition-price withholding on a nonresident seller does not determine the seller's gain base. Apply the actual payment category, payer/recipient status and certificate route, with the conditional nonresident final-tax rule in [Cross-border points](#cross-border-points). That final-tax rule is separate from annual-declaration exemptions and unresolved filing/credit execution.

exact_replacements.before: Art. 25's listed exemptions concern only the specified employment and arts. 119–120 withholding income, or both; it does not list art. 122 capital-payment withholding as a blanket annual-filing exemption.
exact_replacements.after: Art. 25, as corrected by [Order 540/214bis art. 3, printed p. 338](https://amategeko.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BOB_No3-2021.pdf), lists the specified employment and arts. 118–119 withholding income, or both. It does not list art. 122 capital-payment withholding as a blanket annual-filing exemption. This is a separate test from final tax under corrected art. 22.

exact_replacements.before: Both budget replacements of art. 28 retain annual calculation/payment and the deduction for tax paid on art. 37(2) business-asset sales.
exact_replacements.after: Both 2026 budget replacements of art. 28 retain their own enacted annual calculation/payment and credit lists, including tax paid on art. 37(2) business-asset sales. Do not replace those later lists with the 2021 correction of the earlier art. 28.

exact_replacements.before: No treaty exemption or finality of nonresident acquisition withholding is inferred. Mixed/indirect-asset valuation and the interaction of that withholding with the seller's final assessment remain held.
exact_replacements.after: For Burundi-source income of a nonresident that is not attributable to a Burundi PE, IR art. 22 as corrected by [Order 540/214bis art. 3](https://amategeko.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BOB_No3-2021.pdf) makes the withholdings under art. 122 point 4°, art. 123 and art. 125 final. The correction table also replaces art. 22's first cross-reference with arts. 123–125. This does not establish finality for every art. 122 payment, residents or PE-attributable income, and does not itself give an annual-declaration exemption. No treaty exemption is inferred. Mixed/indirect-asset valuation, annual filing/reconciliation and credit execution remain held.
